- When sentiment turns positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >80), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% based on sentiment decay.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over 3+ days, model overconfidently forecasts upward trend; cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 75), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) and price drops, model often undercorrects; add 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong upward momentum, model tends to overproject; cap forecast at 10% below 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.33) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture short-term reversal; use 3-day rolling average to smooth forecast.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a spike, model often lags by 1–2 days; adjust forecast to match true trend 1–2 days ahead.
